page: Microsoft Azure D32als_v6 is a general purpose virtual machine configuration configured with a reduced memory footprint relative to its compute core allocation. Powered by Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, the instance runs on an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz across 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation totals 64.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per thread. The architecture integrates 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside hardware instruction support for AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16), VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration. The instance does not feature local instance storage or bundled GPUs, requiring external Premium Storage volumes for operational disk persistence.

Benchmark assessments demonstrate robust computational processing capabilities, led by strong top-quartile execution in Geekbench single-core (2101.0) and multi-core (18099.0) evaluations, alongside strong stress-ng single-core output (3079.55). Hardware cryptographic performance ranks in the top 25% with a PassMark encryption score of 38609.28, supported by AES instruction sets. Parallel data decompression shows elevated throughput with bzip3 multi-threaded performance reaching 201.75 GB/sec. For lightweight artificial intelligence tasks, the server delivers top-quartile throughput for small 135M parameter language models, sustaining 2524.57 prompt tokens per second and 306.23 text generation tokens per second. Broader metrics, including PassMark CPU aggregate score (46644.2) and Redis SET operations (44.15 million operations per second), register in the middle 50% baseline.

Resource allocation presents clear tradeoffs. The 2.0 GB per vCPU distribution is tailored for computational efficiency rather than memory-heavy datasets, providing lower memory overhead costs for workloads that do not demand typical 1:4 general purpose ratios. The absence of integrated local storage shifts all input and output operations to remote disk targets. This instance profile is well suited for web application serving, batch data processing, distributed compilation, cryptographic workloads, and small model inference services where multi-threaded CPU throughput takes precedence over large working memory allocations.
description: Microsoft Azure D32als_v6 is a general purpose instance configured with a compute-leaning 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Built on AMD EPYC 9V74 x86_64 processors clocked at 3.7 GHz, it provides 32 dedicated vCPUs, 16 physical cores, and 64.0 GB of system memory. The virtual machine includes instruction sets for AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI, but excludes local storage and discrete GPUs. Benchmark results indicate strong top-quartile performance in Geekbench single-core and multi-core tasks, PassMark encryption, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and small-model machine learning inference. Memory bandwidth and standard database transactions align with median platform averages. The constrained 2.0 GB per vCPU memory profile provides cost-effective CPU resource density for workloads such as web servers, CI/CD compilation, and batch data processing where massive memory capacities are unnecessary.
